page.layout: One text column, full width, no marginal notes. Page number and running head at the top. The paragraph continues from the previous page and ends with the hyphenated word "Ferne-liani" set at the right.

main_text.p: folum Fernelius, sed & Galenus statuit: propterea quod tres sunt facultates, naturalis, uitalis, & animalis, quibus totum animal gubernatur. Sed spiritus uitalis his omnibus uiribus potest praeditus esse: propterea dixit Aristoteles lib. de Generatio-ne animalium quinto: spiritum in naturae rebus uariū exhibere ulum. Deinde hepar sanguinem spirituosum gignere non dici-tur. Idcirco nullū per se producit spiritum, sed duntaxat materiam, ex qua ipse a corde fit. Adhaec omnis spiritus animatus esse debet: quandoquidem animae & corporis (ipsimet Fernelio) uinculū est. Sed sanguis hepatis & uenarum nō est animatus, sed naturalis tantum modo corpori alendo destinatus. Ideo animato spiritu caret. Vapor autem ille, qui per phlebotomiam exhalat, pars sanguinis est tenuissima, quae prima diffoluitur. Quod autem ad alium, quae animale medici uocant, spectat, nonnulli medicinae & philosophiae periti ipsum negant esse necessarium: propterea quod animalis facultas absque ulla substantia in neruosas partes ferri, sicut solis radij in haec inferiora possit. Quod sane docet Galenus libro de Locis affectis primo. Fruftra nobis Ferne-liani [?]

page.notes: Page 34 of the printed book, one column, no catchword or signature. The word "liani" at the lower right is the continuation of the hyphenated word "Ferne-", so it belongs to the text, not to a catchword. Doubtful readings: "folum" (a tilde over the u may be printed), "nullū" and "uariū" (macrons unclear), "quae animale" (the "quae" and "animale" spacing is uncertain), "possit" (the last letters are unclear), and "liani" (marked [?]). Old spelling "fpiritus", "fanguis", "ipfe" was converted to plain s.
